Target company: Apple (AAPL). Apple develops and sells personal computing devices including iPhone, Mac and iPad, with operating systems and digital services.

Focal announcement: App Store stopped more than $2 billion in fraudulent transactions in 2022.

Decision cutoff: 2023-05-16T23:59:59-04:00. Use only information available before this cutoff.

Source: App Store stopped more than $2 billion in fraudulent transactions in 2022. Published date: 2023-05-16. URL: https://www.apple.com/newsroom/2023/05/app-store-stopped-more-than-2-billion-in-fraudulent-transactions-in-2022.

Condensed source passage, selected from the supplied excerpt; other details are omitted: The App Store launched in 2008 with the mission of accomplishing two important objectives: to establish a reliable and secure platform for users to safely discover and download apps, and to provide developers with an exciting opportunity to showcase their ideas and grow their business. Today, Apple announced that in 2022, the App Store prevented over $2 billion in potentially fraudulent transactions, and rejected nearly 1.7 million app submissions for failing to meet the App Store’s high standards for privacy, security, and content. Apple detected and blocked more than 147 million fraudulent ratings and reviews from the App Store last year. Apple blocked a record $2 billion in fraudulent transactions in 2022, banning 714,000 fraudulent accounts from transacting again. In total, Apple blocked $2.09 billion in fraudulent transactions on the App Store in 2022.
